info.title: Kletia Platform API
info.summary: Non-custodial, chain-agnostic intents for EVM networks and Solana.
info.description:
Plan cross-network intents into a DAG of network-bound steps, get unsigned wallet-ready transactions, and verify execution from on-chain evidence. Kletia never holds keys. Networks are CAIP-2 ids, accounts CAIP-10, assets CAIP-19, amounts base-unit strings.

Tiers: public 30/min per IP, developer 300/min per key, operator 1200/min per key. Errors are `{ "error": { "code", "message", "issues"?, "hints"?, "details"?, "docs"? }, "requestId" }` with codes from the catalog at GET /v1/errors; every response carries X-Request-Id. Keyed POSTs that create or change state accept `Idempotency-Key`. Agents can use the MCP server at /v1/mcp (read-only tools, plus keyed creation of intents and links; nothing is ever signed). Agent keys (`kl_agt_`) are bound by their rule book chain. Developer and agent keys are server keys: sent from a browser on another origin they get 403 SECRET_KEY_FROM_BROWSER.

post.description: Quotes are advisory and never persisted. Routes are ranked like the planner's bridge auction (guaranteed output net of priced extra costs, then time within `maxSeconds`, then transaction count); `best` is the first eligible route.

Costs one request of the tier limit plus one unit per account of a per-IP budget of 60 account reads per minute (429 RATE_LIMITED after).

post.summary: Plan an intent into an IntentGraph
post.description:
Natural-language `text` is compiled by a deterministic grammar; unsupported wording returns 422 INTENT_UNSUPPORTED with example phrases in `error.hints`. With `dryRun=true` the plan is quoted but not stored (200; Idempotency-Key is ignored). A repeated `clientReference` from the same API key returns the original intent (200).

With `clarify=true` the request is one turn of a task (`IntentTurnRequest`) and Kletia asks instead of refusing: `needs_input` (200) carries at most two questions, assumption chips and a draft; `planned` is 201 when stored (200 on a dry run, or with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` when the turn's clientReference already planned an intent); `cancelled` is 200; a refusal answers its catalogue status and the thread is unchanged. Threads are client-held by default (send `thread` back); `remember: true` (API keys only) keeps them at Kletia (`threadId`, `expectedRev`, `If-Match`). Idempotency-Key also applies to dry-run turns that create or change a Kletia-held thread. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description: Also return the asset-change preview (stage `plan`), simulated from the transactions the quotes already returned; never a failed create (unsimulated steps are quoted).

parameters.name: journey
parameters.description: Also return the journey (where the money is after every step and what follows), built on the plan-stage preview, which it implies; dry runs too. Never a failed create (`journey: null`).

parameters.name: journeyReads
parameters.description: With `journey=true`: `live` (default) reads the accounts' gas and token balances; `none` reads nothing (demo or placeholder accounts).

parameters.name: clarify
parameters.description: Ask instead of refusing: the body is an `IntentTurnRequest` and the response an `IntentTurnResponse` (needs_input 200, planned 201 when stored or 200 on a dry run or a replay, handoff 200, cancelled 200). Without it the endpoint is the strict planner, unchanged. See docs/platform/clarify.md.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: With `clarify=true` and `threadId`: the thread revision the turn expects (as `expectedRev`), e.g. `"3"`; another revision is 409 THREAD_CONFLICT.

200.description: Dry run, or idempotent replay of an existing intent. With `clarify=true`: needs_input, cancelled, a planned dry run or a replayed commit.

201.description: Intent planned and stored (with `clarify=true`: a planned turn that stored its intent).

get.summary: List intents created with the caller's key (or a key below it)

get.summary: Read an intent

post.summary: Build wallet-ready transactions for a ready step
post.description: Every transaction is sent (EVM) or fee-paid (Solana) by the step account. Sign and send them in order, then submit the references. A payload expires at `payload.expiresAt`; prepare again to re-quote. Never retried automatically: an `Idempotency-Key` header is refused with 400 IDEMPOTENCY_NOT_SUPPORTED. The payload is simulated before it is handed out (`payload.preview`, and the whole intent in `preview`); a payload whose simulated effect differs from its step is refused (SIMULATION_FAILED, SIMULATION_ASSET_CHANGE_REFUSED, QUOTE_MOVED, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE). Send `acknowledgedPreview` (the digest of the preview the user approved): a materially worse payload answers 409 PREVIEW_CHANGED with `error.preview`; an unknown digest is not an error (`Kletia-Preview-Ack: unknown`).

parameters.name: journey
parameters.description: Also return the journey at signing time, built on the prepare-stage preview.

Kletia-Preview-Ack.description: Sent when the request carried `acknowledgedPreview`: `matched` (found, nothing material changed) or `unknown` (expired or not kept here; show the fresh `preview`).

post.summary: Submit transaction hashes / signatures for on-chain verification
post.description: A reference advances the step only after Kletia observes it on-chain from the bound account. Same-network steps become `settled`; cross-network steps become `settling` until the settlement network reports the destination fill. References that are provably not this step's transactions are refused with 422 (REFERENCE_WRONG_SENDER, REFERENCE_WRONG_CHAIN, REFERENCE_MISMATCH, REFERENCE_STALE, REFERENCE_ALREADY_USED) and leave the step unchanged. References not yet visible on-chain are stored (`submitted`) and re-verified by refresh and the settlement poller; until one of them produces on-chain evidence, new references (e.g. after a wallet speed-up) replace them. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Re-read verification and settlement state now
Cancel an intent with no submitted steps
post.description: Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of intent events
get.description: Starts with `retry: 3000`, replays buffered events after `Last-Event-ID` (or `?since=`; the whole buffer when absent, or when the id is no longer buffered, so de-duplicate by event id), then streams live events. Each frame is `id: <event id>`, `event: <type>`, `data: <KletiaEvent JSON>`. A comment heartbeat is sent every 15 s and the stream ends after 30 minutes.

200.description: Event stream. Every `data` line is a KletiaEvent (see components.schemas.KletiaEvent).

text/event-stream.example:
retry: 3000

id: evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
event: intent.created
data: {"id":"evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","type":"intent.created","at":"2026-10-08T12:00:00.000Z","data":{"intentId":"int_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","summary":{}}}

get.summary: Server-Sent Events stream of the key's events (routed like its webhooks)
get.description: Every event that would be delivered to the key's webhooks (intent, receipt, contract, link, Rule Book and key events), as `id`, `event` and `data` frames where `data` is the webhook envelope `{ id, type, at, data }`. `scope=subtree` adds the events of the key's descendant agent keys (and project-wide rule book events on project keys), like webhooks created with `scope: "subtree"`. Starts with `retry: 3000`; `Last-Event-ID` (or `?since=`) replays the matching events after that id from this instance's buffer (500 events, 10 minutes; an id no longer buffered replays the whole buffer, so de-duplicate by event id); without it the stream starts with live events. A heartbeat comment every 15 s re-checks the key (a revoked or expired key's stream ends); a stream lasts at most 30 minutes. At most 2 open streams per key (429 TOO_MANY_STREAMS).

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated event types (default: every type).

200.description: Event stream. Every `data` line is a KletiaEvent (see components.schemas.KletiaEvent).

text/event-stream.example:
retry: 3000

id: evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
event: link.created
data: {"id":"evt_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","type":"link.created","at":"2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z","data":{"linkId":"lk_0123456789abcdef01234567","ownerKeyId":"key_0123456789abcdef01234567","revision":1}}

get.summary: Where the money is after every step, and what follows
get.description: The journey of a stored intent on its latest preview (recomputed when older than 60 s and the intent is not finished): stops with holdings, legs with refund paths, and consequences by severity with options. Results are cached for 15 s. At most 30 reads per intent per minute on top of the tier limit; `refresh=true` bypasses the cache at most once per 10 s per intent. Fetch it with the plan and when a step changes (intent events), not on a timer.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Read the facts again instead of serving the 15 s cache.

parameters.name: reads
parameters.description: `none` skips every account read.

post.summary: End an intent at its current stop
post.description: Every step not started (or failed) is skipped; the money stays where the journey says (stopping never moves money). Nothing started: the intent is `cancelled`; otherwise `partially_completed` once a step settled. Idempotent. Refused with 409 INTENT_IN_FLIGHT (retryable, `Retry-After`) while a step is submitted, settling or under review, or holds a prepared payload that can still be signed (until it expires). Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key).

post.summary: Mint a model-assisted reading consent token
post.description: Browser callers only (the Kletia desk, or a publishable key of a project with `modelReading: "enabled"` from one of its allowed origins); server keys get 403 CONFIRM_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED, so an agent can never consent or confirm for the person. `once` covers one message (bound to its text and the wallet), `session` 8 hours of typed desk text, `confirm` the person's "Yes, plan it" on a model reading of one thread.

get.summary: List the key's Kletia-held clarify threads
get.description: Threads created with `remember: true` by this API key that have not expired, most recently used first. Publishable keys and the public tier have no Kletia-held threads.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` of the previous page.

get.summary: Read a Kletia-held clarify thread
get.description: The thread blob, its context, its last response and its intents. Another key's thread, or an expired one, is 404 THREAD_NOT_FOUND.

delete.description: The row is removed at once; later turns on it get 404 THREAD_NOT_FOUND. Intents it planned are not affected.

post.summary: Recompute an intent's asset-change preview
post.description: Simulates the transactions the plan's quotes already returned (or quotes steps that cannot be simulated) and aggregates the whole intent: what leaves your wallets, what arrives, fees, approvals and what your wallets must hold. No provider is called unless `quotes=refresh` (ready steps re-quoted, once per 20 s per intent, at most 4 steps). At most 6 recomputations per intent per minute (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After). Takes no body.

get.summary: The last preview computed for an intent
get.description: Any stage (plan, prepare, refresh), kept for 30 minutes. 404 PREVIEW_NOT_FOUND when none is kept.

get.summary: The intent's latest receipt with every disclosure
get.description: Receipts are issued after the intent ends (completed, partially completed, failed or cancelled) and every on-chain reference is finalized, usually 15 to 25 minutes after the last leg on EVM rollups, seconds on Solana and Polygon. 202 with `pending` and Retry-After while waiting; 409 RECEIPT_NOT_READY while the intent runs (when no earlier receipt exists), 409 RECEIPT_NOT_APPLICABLE for expired intents, 503 RECEIPTS_DISABLED when the deployment cannot sign. `sequence` reads an earlier receipt (404 RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND when unknown).

200.description: Receipt (with `pending` when a newer state is being receipted).

get.summary: Every receipt sequence of an intent

post.summary: Share a receipt (link returned once)
post.description: Encrypts the chosen disclosure groups with a fresh key that only the returned `url` carries (in its fragment); Kletia keeps the ciphertext, never the key. At most 10 active shares per receipt (409 RECEIPT_SHARE_LIMIT); 410 RECEIPT_DISCLOSURES_WITHDRAWN after a withdrawal. Honours `Idempotency-Key` with an API key: the stored response (with the link) is encrypted at rest.

get.summary: Active shares of the intent's receipts (no keys)

delete.summary: Withdraw stored disclosures and every share
delete.description: Deletes the stored disclosures of every receipt of the intent (and of later ones) and every share. The signed payloads (commitments only) and log leaves stay; copies already downloaded cannot be recalled. 409 RECEIPT_NOT_READY (or RECEIPT_NOT_APPLICABLE) when the intent has no receipt yet.

get.summary: Receipt signing keys and EAS attesters
get.description: Ed25519 public keys (active, next, retired, revoked; development keys sign only outside production). Cacheable for 60 minutes. Cross-check with the web origin's /.well-known/kletia-receipt-keys.json before trusting a key that is not pinned in @kletia/core.

get.summary: Transparency log batches
get.description: Hourly batches: an RFC 6962 Merkle tree over receipt digests, hash-chained and signed. `unanchored=true` lists batches no EAS timestamp on Base is recorded for yet.

get.summary: Inclusion proof of a receipt digest
One log batch (optionally its leaves)

post.summary: Report the Base transaction that timestamped a batch (operator)
post.description: Recorded only when the transaction is a successful call to EAS.timestamp(batchDigest) on Base whose timestamp EAS returns (422 RECEIPT_ANCHOR_INVALID otherwise, 409 RECEIPT_ANCHOR_EXISTS when already recorded). Kletia only reads the chain.

get.summary: A shared receipt's signed payload
get.description: Only while the owner shares the receipt; unknown and unshared receipts both answer 404 RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND. No disclosures (they come encrypted from the share).

get.summary: Whether a shared receipt was superseded
A share's encrypted disclosures
get.description: Decrypt with the key from the link's fragment (Web Crypto AES-GCM), then verify with verifyReceipt. 404 RECEIPT_SHARE_NOT_FOUND when unknown or revoked, 410 RECEIPT_SHARE_EXPIRED when expired.

post.summary: Issue an agent key under a key (kl_agt_…, secret returned once)
post.description: Agent keys sit at most 3 levels below a project key (409 KEY_DEPTH_EXCEEDED), at most 100 active per project (409 AGENT_KEY_LIMIT_REACHED), always expire and never outlive their parent. Their rule book (policy or template) is version 1; without one they are observers. Every request of an agent key is checked against its whole chain, and revoking a key revokes its subtree. Project keys only: an agent key with `permissions.createChildKeys` requests a sub-agent instead (POST /v1/agents/{id}/subagents), which a human approves. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (the stored response is encrypted at rest).

201.description: The agent key with its secret.

get.summary: Read a key's rule book
get.description: The key's own rule book (active version and pending amendment) and the effective chain it is evaluated against. Keys in the caller's subtree only (project keys: the whole project).

put.summary: Create or replace a key's rule book
put.description: Tightening applies at once; loosening waits `amendments.delaySeconds` (status `pending`, `policy.amendment_pending` webhook), and a newer write supersedes a pending one. Project keys with their current secret only; agent keys never write rule books (403 AGENT_KEY_FORBIDDEN). Invalid documents: 400 POLICY_INVALID with issues; a stale If-Match: 409 POLICY_CONFLICT. Honours `Idempotency-Key`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The current rule book hash (`"sha256:…"`, as the ETag), or `none` when there is none. A mismatch is refused with 409 POLICY_CONFLICT. Absent: unconditional.

ETag.description: The new rule book hash (`"sha256:…"`) for If-Match.

delete.description: Removal is a loosening: it waits for the amendment delay like any loosening (an agent key without a rule book is an observer). Returns the removal version.

post.summary: Validate a rule book (and compare it with another)
post.description: Public and stateless: the same checks as validatePolicy in @kletia/core, the canonical hash, warnings, and with `against` what the change tightens and loosens.

post.summary: Simulate a request against a key's chain
post.description: Plans the request as a dry run under the effective constraints and explains every rule (pass, fail, trigger, warn), with spend usage and the timetable. Optionally replaces the key's own rule book with a draft, or moves the clock. Nothing is stored, reserved or held; the decision log records an `evaluate` entry. 30 per minute per key.

get.summary: The hash-chained decision log
get.description: Every plan, prepare, submit, evaluation, approval, amendment and key decision of the caller's subtree, newest first. Records are chained per project (verifyDecisionChain in @kletia/core).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Page after this decision id.

get.summary: One decision
Spend windows of a key's chain
get.description: Rolling 24 h and 7 d USD usage and what remains at every level (project, ancestors, the key).

get.summary: Approvals requested by (or waiting for) the caller
Read an approval (the id is the capability)
get.description: What the held intent does (steps, recipients, value, ceiling, triggers) and what to sign. Reading is not approving. Wallets are masked.

post.summary: Approve a held intent
post.description: With an empty body, the request's API key decides (an active project key outside the requester's subtree, listed in `confirm.approvers.keys` when the list is set; agent keys never approve). With `{ account, signature, expiresAt }`, a listed approver wallet decides (EIP-712, ERC-1271 or ERC-6492 on EVM; a signed message on Solana). A decision is final (409 APPROVAL_DECIDED).

post.summary: Reject a held intent (it is cancelled)
post.description: Same deciders as approve.

post.summary: Publish an intent link
post.description: A public link (`/go/lk_…`) whose destination the publisher fixes and whose funding the visitor chooses (networks, assets, amount within bounds). Validated like validateLinkDefinition, recipient names resolved and pinned, contracts pinned at their active revision, checked against the key's rule book (422 LINK_POLICY_CONFLICT) and dry-run planned for a representative funding choice. Production links that pay a fixed third party or call a custom contract are `pending` for 15 minutes. Unverified publishers are capped at $1000 per intent. At most 200 active links and 60 creations an hour per key. Agent keys need `permissions.links`. Honours `Idempotency-Key`.

get.summary: Links of the caller (and its subtree)
Read a link
get.description: Public view for anyone; the owner's view (definition, pins, reasons, totals) for the owning key, its ancestors and the project's project keys. A link whose owning key was revoked is not found.

patch.summary: Tighten, pause or resume a link
patch.description: Every change only narrows what visitors can do (new revision, `link.updated`); pausing and resuming (`link.paused`). A link that paused itself because a pinned name or contract changed resumes only with `accept` (409 LINK_RECIPIENT_CHANGED / LINK_CONTRACT_CHANGED otherwise) and is re-pinned. Honours `Idempotency-Key`.

delete.description: Visitors get 410 LINK_EXPIRED; intents already started can finish. Idempotent.

post.summary: Quote a link for a funding choice (nothing stored)
post.description: The dry-run intent and its preview for the visitor's choice; without accounts the quote is indicative. Cached 20 s per choice (`Kletia-Quote-Cache: hit`). 20 per minute per IP and 300 per link.

post.summary: Create the visitor's intent from a link
post.description: Plans and stores the intent the link describes for the visitor's accounts, owned by the link's key (its rule book applies; `metadata.linkId` forces strict simulation at prepare). A use is reserved at the first prepare and consumed at the first submit; abandoned intents release it. The plan must stay inside the link's envelope (fixed networks, recipients, contracts and input) or nothing is stored. 10 per minute per IP, 120 per link and 5 per 10 minutes per account.

200.description: An intent stored earlier with this clientReference.

get.summary: Privacy-preserving counters of a link
Share card (PNG)
get.description: The link as a ticket: title, route, publisher, domain seal, amount bounds and expiry. `wide` 1200x600 (og:image), `square` 600x600 (blink icon). Cached per revision (ETag; `?v=<revision>` is immutable). No live counters. 600 page and card requests per minute per link.

parameters.name: v
parameters.description: The link revision (cache busting).

get.summary: The link page shell with per-link meta (served at /go/{id} by the web origin)
get.description: The web app's HTML shell with the link's title, description, card image and canonical URL injected (escaped) for unfurls; the page itself renders client-side. Unknown, withdrawn or suspended links get a noindex page. 503 LINK_PAGE_UNAVAILABLE (HTML) when the shell cannot be loaded.

schema.description: lk_ followed by 24 hex characters (anything else renders the not-found page).

post.summary: Report a link (counted, no free text)
post.description: 5 per hour per IP. Reports are counters the operator reviews; nothing personal is stored.

post.summary: Suspend a link (operator)
post.description: Operator keys only. Every prepare of the link's intents is refused (409 LINK_SUSPENDED); `link.suspended`.

post.summary: Approve or revoke a link's blink (operator)

post.description: Checks the order, picks the protocol (Solana: Jupiter Trigger for limit, Jupiter Recurring for DCA; Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base: CoW Protocol limit orders, TWAP for DCA) and compares it with the market. Nothing is stored. At most 30 quotes, preparations and cancels per minute from one address.

post.summary: Prepare what the owner signs
post.description: Jupiter: an unsigned transaction built by Jupiter and checked by Kletia (fee payer and sole signer, programs, compute budget). CoW limit: an approval of the GPv2VaultRelayer when the allowance is short, then the EIP-712 order. CoW TWAP: Safe transactions (only a Safe set up for ComposableCoW can create one; a plain account gets 422 ORDER_UNSUPPORTED with error.details.reason `twap-requires-safe`). Preparations live briefly on the instance that made them. At most 30 quotes, preparations and cancels per minute from one address.

post.summary: Relay the owner's signature
post.description: Fail closed: a signed Solana transaction must carry byte for byte the prepared message (its sha256) and a valid signature of the owner, and nothing else is signed; an EIP-712 signature must recover to the owner over the prepared digest (ERC-1271 `isValidSignature` for contract owners). Otherwise 422 ORDER_SIGNATURE_MISMATCH and nothing is relayed. Then Kletia relays exactly that: Jupiter's `/execute`, or the CoW orderbook. Repeating the relayed submission returns the same result (Idempotent-Replayed); another signature for a used preparation is 409 ORDER_PREPARATION_USED.

post.description: With the agent key `{id}` itself, whose chain grants `permissions.createChildKeys`. The rule book must be a subset of the parent's whole chain; sub-agents never get webhooks, registerContracts, sessions or links, and every permission not asked for is off. At most 3 levels below a project key (409 KEY_DEPTH_EXCEEDED), 10 children and open requests per parent and 5 open requests (409 SUBAGENT_LIMIT_REACHED). The request stays open 24 h. Emits agent.subagent_requested. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (stored sealed: the answer carries the claim token).

201.description: The request and its claim token (shown once).

get.summary: Requests and sub-agents of a key
get.description: The key `{id}` must be the caller or in its subtree (project keys: any key of the project).

200.description: Requests newest first, and the live children with caps and use.

get.summary: The agent tree with caps, use and requests
get.description: Project keys: every project and agent key of the project; agent keys: themselves and their subtree. Each node shows its mode, the strictest mode of its chain, caps and rolling 24 h / 7 d use (children's spending counts in every ancestor's windows).

get.summary: Open requests for a wallet's projects (a count)
get.description: Public. Answers only how many open sub-agent requests wait in projects the wallet owns, so the desk can tell the connected wallet; names, ids and projects are never shown here.

get.summary: A sub-agent request
get.description: What is granted, line by line beside the parent's own rule book. Keys of the request's subtree and project keys read it.

post.summary: The message the owner wallet signs
post.description: From the Kletia developer portal (first-party Origin, else 403 ACCOUNT_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN), for the wallet that owns the project only (403 SUBAGENT_APPROVER_NOT_ALLOWED). The message names the domain, the wallet, the decision, the request, project, parent, rule book hash, caps, networks, actions, permissions and the key's expiry, with a single-use nonce valid 10 minutes. A new message replaces the previous one.

post.summary: Approve: mint the sub-agent
post.description: With a project key of the project (empty body, current secret) or the owner wallet's `{ message, signature }` from the same origin as the challenge (the nonce is used up first; 403 SUBAGENT_SIGNATURE_INVALID otherwise; 502 RPC_UNAVAILABLE when a smart account cannot be checked). The parent's chain is read again (409 SUBAGENT_PARENT_INACTIVE, 403 SUBAGENT_POLICY_NOT_SUBSET). Mints the key once with a secret nobody sees; the requester claims it within 15 minutes. Emits key.created and agent.subagent_approved.

200.description: The approved request with childKeyId and claimBy.

post.summary: Deny a sub-agent request
post.description: Same deciders and signature rules as approve. A decision is final (409 SUBAGENT_REQUEST_DECIDED). Emits agent.subagent_denied.

post.summary: Claim the approved sub-agent's key (once)
post.description: With the requesting parent's key and the claim token (compared in constant time). Sets a fresh secret and returns it once. A wrong token, a second claim or a claim after the 15-minute window is 403 SUBAGENT_CLAIM_INVALID; a late claim revokes the unclaimed key. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (stored sealed).

post.summary: Revoke an agent and its subtree
post.description: Project keys: any agent key of the project; agent keys: their descendants only. Everything below stops at once. Emits key.revoked and agent.subagent_revoked.

post.summary: Pause an agent (and its subtree)
post.description: Project keys only. Writes `mode: "paused"` into the key's rule book, a tightening that applies at once; every descendant reads its chain fresh and stops too. Resume from the Rule Book (a loosening waits the amendment delay).

post.summary: Register a webhook (secret returned once)
post.description: At most 10 webhooks per key. Deliveries are signed with `Kletia-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<t>.<raw body>")>`; verify with verifyWebhookSignature from @kletia/core. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response (with the secret) is encrypted at rest.

get.summary: List webhooks

delete.summary: Delete a webhook (and its delivery log)

post.summary: Send a signed webhook.test event now
post.description: Makes one synchronous delivery attempt of a `webhook.test` event (see the webhookTest webhook) with the same signing, network rules, 5 s timeout and no-redirect policy as real deliveries, records it in the delivery log and returns the outcome. Always 200 when the attempt was made, whatever the endpoint answered. Test deliveries never pause a webhook. At most 5 per minute per webhook.

get.summary: Delivery log of a webhook
get.description: Every attempt, drop and test delivery, newest first. Payloads and error text are never stored. Kept for 7 days (at most 1000 per webhook; 100 with in-memory storage).

post.summary: Issue a developer key
post.description: The key is shown once and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. Without a key this starts a new project; with a developer key the new key joins the caller's project (at most 5 active keys, else 409 KEY_LIMIT_REACHED). Limited to 5 keys per hour per IP; a request refused with a 4xx (an invalid body, a key limit) does not count. `sandbox: true` issues a key kept on the testnet lane by its own rule book. Body: `{ "name": "acme-dev", "sandbox": true }`. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response is encrypted at rest.

get.summary: List the keys of the caller's project
get.description: Never returns secrets, only `last4`. Operator keys cannot be listed (409 KEY_NOT_MANAGEABLE); a secret inside its rotation grace window cannot manage keys (403 KEY_SECRET_ROTATED).

post.summary: Replace a key's secret (same id)
post.description: Issues a new secret for an active key of the caller's project. The key id is unchanged, so intents, webhooks and usage stay attached. The previous secret keeps authenticating for `graceSeconds` (default 24 h, at most 7 days, 0 = stop now) but cannot manage keys; rotating again ends an earlier grace window. Other instances notice within 15 s. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The stored response is encrypted at rest and replayed only to the current secret or to the secret that made the request (a key that rotated itself can retry with its old secret during the grace window); any other rotated-out secret gets 403 KEY_SECRET_ROTATED.

200.description: The key with its new secret.

delete.summary: Revoke a key of the caller's project
delete.description: Idempotent. The key and every agent key below it (its subtree) stop authenticating at once on the answering instance and within 15 s everywhere (`key.revoked` lists the cascade). A key may revoke itself. Its webhooks and their delivery logs are deleted and its intents' events are no longer delivered; repeating the call finishes a cleanup that failed (503).

patch.description: Shortening applies at once (descendants never outlive it). Extending is a loosening: refused while the key's rule book has an amendment delay. Agent keys always expire; project keys may clear it with null. Managed keys only (the caller's subtree).

get.summary: Requests, status classes and intents of the caller's key
get.description: Counts every request made with the key, by hour, route and status class (flushed every 30 s), plus the live rate-limit window of the answering instance and the intents the key created in the window.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: `subtree`: add per-key attribution of the caller's subtree (project keys: every key of the project).

post.summary: Register a custom contract (EVM) or Solana Actions endpoint
post.description: Validates the definition (the same rules as validateContractDefinition in @kletia/core: forbidden functions, argument and event bindings, reserved names, deny lists), pins the code identity on-chain (code hash, proxy implementation; Solana program data, deploy slot, upgrade authority), records source (Sourcify) / program (OtterSec) verification and, for Solana, each action's metadata. Mainnet registrations stay `pending` for the activation delay (default 15 minutes; testnets activate at once) and send `contract.registered` then `contract.activated` webhooks; integrator names that use a reserved brand also wait for domain verification. At most 25 registrations per key; registrations, updates and reverifications share 20 per hour per key. A rotated-out secret cannot register (403 KEY_SECRET_ROTATED). Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.summary: List the caller's registrations and its project's visible ones
What registering an address or programs would pin and allow
get.description: EVM (`network` + `address`): deployment, EIP-7702 delegation, deny-list reason, pins with proxy detection, Sourcify status and ABI, every function marked allowed or forbidden with the reason, and `hints.erc4626` (`asset()` read once, with its registry symbol) when the ABI is an ERC-4626 vault. Solana (`network` + `programs`, comma separated): program pins, deny-list reasons and OtterSec status. Nothing is stored. Shares 20 calls per minute per key with the test endpoint.

get.summary: Read a registration
get.description: The owner also gets the ABI (or programs and payees) and the revision history. Unknown ids and other keys' private registrations both answer 404 CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND.

patch.description: Labels and phrases change in place. Any other change is re-validated, re-pinned and stored as a new revision: pending for the activation delay on mainnet (the active revision keeps serving until then; intents planned on it stop preparing once the new one activates, 409 CONTRACT_REVISION_CHANGED), immediate on testnets. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

delete.description: Planned intents that use it stop preparing (409 CONTRACT_NOT_USABLE); verification of submitted steps continues.

post.summary: Dry-run an action for an account (simulation + review)
post.description: Runs the plan and prepare pipeline of one entry for `account` (the owner tests the latest revision, also while it is pending): bindings, approvals, simulation and the review users will see. Never stored, never signed, and the response carries no calldata to persist. 20 per minute per key (shared with inspect).

post.summary: Re-read pins and verification after an intended upgrade (owner only)
post.description: Re-pins the code, re-checks Sourcify / OtterSec and the domain file (`/.well-known/kletia.json` listing the id). Changed pins, or a suspension for pins_changed, program_changed or outcome_mismatch, create a new revision (pending on mainnet; the registration becomes active again when it activates). Unchanged code only refreshes the verification. Operator suspensions cannot be lifted here. Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

post.summary: Suspend any registration (operator key)
post.description: Abuse handling. Sends contract.suspended to the owner's webhooks; the owner cannot lift it.

post.summary: Create a session the embed turns into an intent for a visitor
post.description: A fixed template of structured actions (custom contract steps of the caller's registrations included), the origins allowed to embed it, an optional visitor-chosen amount within bounds, a TTL and a use count. The template is planned once as a dry run, so a broken template fails here. The response's `embedUrl` carries the id in the URL fragment. At most 1000 active sessions per key (429 RATE_LIMITED beyond). A registration that is still pending (mainnet activation delay) adds `warnings: [{ code: "CONTRACT_PENDING", contract, activatesAt }]`; a session that would expire before it activates is refused with 422 SESSION_EXPIRES_BEFORE_ACTIVATION (`details.minimumExpiresInSeconds`). Every session intent counts in the owner key's own Rule Book spend windows. With a publishable key, send only `{ flow, hostOrigin }`: a single-use 600 s session from the project's stored flow, owned by the publishable key, whose call / action steps use the registrations of the key that saved the flow (404 FLOW_UNKNOWN; 403 PUBLISHABLE_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN when hostOrigin is not an allowed origin). Honours `Idempotency-Key` (with an API key): a retry with the same key and request replays the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`.

get.summary: Session view for the embed (public; the id is the capability)
get.description: Integrator identity, allowed origins, action labels, amount bounds, status and expiry, and `warnings` while a registration of the template is still pending. Never the key or the project.

post.summary: Turn a session into an intent for the visitor's accounts (public)
post.description: Re-checks expiry (410 SESSION_EXPIRED), the use count (409 SESSION_USED; one atomic use) and that `hostOrigin` is an allowed origin (403 SESSION_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN), then plans the template with the visitor's accounts under the session owner's key, with `metadata.sessionId` set. A plan that fails gives the use back. The visitor reviews and signs every step in their own wallet.

200.description: The intent this visitor already created with the session's clientReference.

get.summary: Error catalog
get.description: Every error code the API returns, and every step failure code, with its status, category, retryability and remedy. Cacheable for 5 minutes.

get.summary: API status badge
get.description: operational / degraded / down from the health report. SVG by default; `format=shields` returns a shields.io endpoint document for `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=<encoded URL>`. Cacheable for 60 seconds.

post.summary: Model Context Protocol server (Streamable HTTP)
post.description: MCP revision 2026-07-28, plus stateless serving of 2025-era clients that open with `initialize`. Send one JSON-RPC message per request with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; batches are refused and GET answers 405 (no server-initiated stream). Tools: `list_networks`, `list_protocols`, `list_assets`, `get_quote`, `plan_intent`, `get_intent`, `list_intents`, `get_portfolio`, `create_signing_link`, `list_contracts`, `get_contract`, `test_contract_action`, `preview_intent`, `get_journey`, `get_receipt`, `get_policy`, `check_intent`, `create_intent`, `get_approval`, `list_links`, `get_link`, `quote_link`, `create_link`, `request_subagent`, `list_subagents`, `claim_subagent`, `revoke_subagent`, `search_prediction_markets`, `plan_prediction_order`. Every tool is read-only except `create_intent` (stores an intent within the key's rule book; agent keys need `permissions.mcpCreateIntents`) and `create_link` (publishes a link; `permissions.links`). No tool prepares, signs or submits a transaction; `create_signing_link` returns a Studio link (text up to 500 characters) for the user to sign with their own wallet. An API key maps to the MCP auth info (`clientId` = key id). Requests with an `Origin` header must come from an HTTPS origin (or localhost in development), else 403 MCP_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN. Add it to Claude Code with `claude mcp add --transport http kletia https://api.kletiaai.xyz/v1/mcp`.

200.description: JSON-RPC response (application/json), or an event stream for 2025-era requests.

400.description: A JSON-RPC error for a batch, a body that is not one JSON-RPC message, an unsupported protocol revision or MCP headers that disagree with the body; the platform error envelope (INVALID_JSON) for a body that is not JSON.

404.description: A JSON-RPC error (-32601) for an unknown method on the 2026-07-28 revision.

406.description: A JSON-RPC error when Accept does not list both application/json and text/event-stream.

500.description: A JSON-RPC error (-32603) when the MCP server fails; the platform error envelope (INTERNAL_ERROR) for a failure before it.

get.summary: This OpenAPI document

post.summary: Intent event delivery
post.description: Sent for intents created with your API key to each matching webhook. Respond 2xx within 5 seconds; redirects are not followed. Failed deliveries are retried up to 3 times (after 1 s, 5 s and 25 s). Each key's deliveries are queued separately (at most 200 waiting; the oldest is dropped beyond that) and a webhook receives one delivery at a time. A webhook whose last 5 attempts failed is paused for 30 s, doubling up to 5 minutes while it keeps failing; its deliveries wait meanwhile. With Postgres the queue is durable: retries survive restarts, so an event can arrive more than once (deduplicate by Kletia-Event-Id). `intent.receipt_issued` is sent once a receipt is issued (after every reference is finalized; ids and digest only); webhooks created before it existed do not receive it unless re-created.

post.summary: Contract registration event delivery
post.description: Sent to the webhooks of the registration's own key that subscribe to the type: contract.registered (a registration or a new revision; on mainnet it activates after the delay), contract.activated, contract.suspended (pins changed, outcome mismatch, program changed, domain no longer verified, operator) and contract.reactivated. Same signing, retries and queueing as intent events. Webhooks created before these types existed do not receive them unless re-created.

post.summary: Intent link event delivery
post.description: Sent to the webhooks of the link's owning key that subscribe to the type (and to `scope: "subtree"` webhooks of its ancestors): link.created, link.activated, link.updated (tightened, domain verified or not, blink approval), link.paused (by the publisher, or itself when a pinned name or contract changed), link.suspended, link.exhausted, link.expired, link.deleted. Same signing, retries and queueing as intent events.

post.summary: Automation event delivery
post.description: Sent to the webhooks of the automation's owning key that subscribe to the type (and to `scope: "subtree"` webhooks of its ancestors): automation.created, automation.updated (paused, resumed, label or limits changed, completed, expired), automation.deleted, automation.fired (a run planned an intent: `needs_signature`, or `prepared` by a native order provider), automation.skipped (a limit, `reason`) and automation.failed (`reason`: the error code). Wallet-owned automations send none. Same signing, retries and queueing as intent events.

post.summary: Rule Book and key event delivery
post.description: Sent to the subject key's webhooks, to `scope: "subtree"` webhooks of its ancestors and to `scope: "subtree"` webhooks of the project's project keys: policy.violation, policy.approval_requested, policy.approval_decided, policy.amendment_pending, policy.amended, policy.spend_threshold (80 % and 95 % of a window), key.created, key.revoked (with the cascade) and the sub-agent events agent.subagent_requested, agent.subagent_approved, agent.subagent_denied and agent.subagent_revoked (subject: the parent key).

post.summary: Test delivery
post.description: Sent once by POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test, signed like every delivery. Never retried. Acknowledge with any 2xx.

bearerAuth.description: Developer, agent or operator API key; or a publishable key (kl_pub_, browsers: only the operations the Projects tag lists, from the project's allowed origins).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the first response with this key (per API key) is stored for 24 hours and replayed for the same request. The same key with a different request → 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; while the first request runs → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS (Retry-After: 1; an abandoned reservation is taken over after 120 s). 5xx, 429 and retryable errors are never stored. Requires an API key (400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRES_API_KEY).

X-Request-Id.description: Request id (echoes a valid incoming UUID).

Idempotent-Replayed.description: `true` when the response replays an earlier request (Idempotency-Key or clientReference).

retryable.description: True when repeating the same request later can succeed without changing it.

families.description: Dynamic provider codes and the catalog entry describing them.

from.description: Input asset: symbol on `network`, address/mint or CAIP-19 id.

amount.description: Decimal amount of `from`, or `max` (on a dependent step: the guaranteed output of the previous step).

recipient.description: Address or CAIP-10 account. Defaults to the acting account.

contract.description: `call` / `action` only (required there): a contract registration id (ct_…) or one of its aliases. Only intents created with the registration's key (or a key of its project, for project-visible registrations) can use it.

examples: bridge 25 USDC from base to solana then swap half to JitoSOL

sourceNetwork.description: Where the money starts. A network key: the first action spends funds there, and when it runs on another network the planner adds a bridge from this one first (a transfer elsewhere, an input the network does not have, or another capital lane is 422 SOURCE_UNREACHABLE). `auto`: the planner picks a network whose accounts hold enough of the first action's input (422 SOURCE_REQUIRED with `details.candidates` when a bridge has no source and nobody holds enough). A sentence that names the network wins. A network key also serves as `defaultNetwork` when that is absent. Absent: unchanged behaviour. See `interpretation.departure`.

clientReference.description: Idempotency key (honoured for callers with an API key).

quoteBinding.description: SHA-256 binding of the prepared transactions.

to.description: EVM call target; for Solana steps, the program invoked.

recipientName.description: Name the recipient was resolved from (ENS, Basenames, SNS); resolved again before every prepare.

venue.description: Registry venue id (e.g. base:aave-v3:usdc) a deposit or withdraw executes against.

extraCosts.description: Value paid on top of the input, such as a bridge's fixed native fee.

references.description: Submitted transaction hashes / signatures, in order.

gasTopup.description: Gas delivered with a cross-network fill (`constraints.gasOnArrival`, Relay); never bound on-chain, the step settles on its main output.

observedCredit.description: Set on a failed leg when the destination credited less than the floor: that amount is in the recipient's wallet.

chosen.description: `text`: the sentence named it; `request`: sourceNetwork; `auto`: chosen by balance; `inferred`: no hint was given.

bridged.description: True when the planner added a bridge from `network` in front of the first action.
